name: pentagi
description: Fully autonomous AI Agents system capable of performing complex penetration testing tasks
one_liner: A self-hosted team of AI agents that tests whether your own computer systems can be hacked, and hands you a report, instead of hiring a team of human hackers.
buyer: A security engineer or managed-security provider who currently pays expensive human penetration testers for routine, repeatable security checks.
business_use_cases: A mid-size company runs it internally before every major release to catch common vulnerabilities without booking an expensive outside pentest each time.
A managed security service provider (MSSP) uses it to run a first-pass automated pentest across many client environments, reserving human experts for deeper follow-up.
A cybersecurity bootcamp or training company uses it as a safe, controlled sandbox for students to see how real attack chains are planned and executed.

money_ideas.idea: Run a 'continuous automated pentesting' managed service for companies that only get a human pentest once a year, billed monthly per environment.
Sell the vendor's own Enterprise tier (reports, plugins, attack-chain view) as the upsell path for teams that outgrow the open-source core.

steal_this: Offer a one-off 'automated pentest report' for small SaaS companies that can't afford a traditional pentest, delivered in days instead of weeks, as a lead-in to the recurring service.
